title: Elysee, Grand Large and Monthlery: reading the true versions of the Aronde 1300
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: The Aronde 1300 designation covers cars that differ quite noticeably in presentation and public. To avoid confusion, each name needs to be placed back inside Simca’s range logic.
content:
Once one speaks of the Aronde 1300, it is easy to mix everything together. Yet an Elysee saloon, a more stylistic Grand Large and a Monthlery loaded with endurance memory do not tell the same story.

Elysee as the central saloon reading

The Elysee often stands for the version most readily found in family memory. It remains the readable saloon, well placed and representative enough to carry the general image of the Aronde 1300.

That is also what makes it important: it sets the reading norm around which the other versions take their place.

Grand Large and Monthlery, two ways of widening the model

Grand Large pushes style further, while Monthlery adds to the model’s image a memory of endurance and performance. One is therefore dealing not only with trims, but with different tonalities inside the range.

These nuances matter in collecting. They change interest, perceived rarity and sometimes the restoration budget.

Always verify the car’s real coherence

As often with Simca, the names can seduce easily. One still has to return to the car itself: body, interior, fittings, period and available documentation.

The right version is not only the one with the attractive label. It is the one whose overall coherence still holds without tricks.

This note extends the page the Simca Aronde 1300. Within the same cluster, the next useful step is The Aronde 1300 Flash engine: what it really brings to Simca.
